name: Pulmonary Valve Agenesis with Intact Ventricular Septum and Persistent Ductus Arteriosus Syndrome
aliases: Pulmonary Valve Agenesis-Intact Ventricular Septum-Persistent Ductus Arteriosus Complex

criteria.description: Absence of pulmonary valve leaflets confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
No ventricular septal defect detected on imaging studies
Presence of patent ductus arteriosus confirmed by echocardiography or angiography
Clinical evidence of central cyanosis in neonatal period

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pulmonary valve agenesis, intact ventricular septum, and persistent ductus arteriosus confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic and angiographic findings in the neonatal period.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central cyanosis due to right-to-left shunting
searchTerms: blue skin from heart blood mixing
central cyanosis due to heart shunt

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic murmur due to turbulent flow across PDA
searchTerms: heart noise from turbulent blood flow

pathognomonic.symptomName: Right ventricular hypertrophy secondary to outflow obstruction
searchTerms: thickened right ventricle due to blockage
right heart muscle enlargement from outflow blockage
failure to gain weight as baby

common.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to right heart failure
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart failure
poor exercise tolerance in young children
too much blood flow to lungs
neurological issues due to lack of oxygen
nerve symptoms caused by low blood oxygen

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating absence of pulmonary valve leaflets, intact ventricular septum, and patent ductus arteriosus
Cardiac MRI confirming right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary artery anatomy
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Electrocardiogram showing right ventricular hypertrophy and possible arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pulmonary valve leaflets with stenosis rather than agenesis
Overriding aorta and right ventricular outflow tract obstruction

redFlags: Severe neonatal cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in the first weeks of life
Progressive respiratory distress with poor feeding and failure to thrive
references: Anderson RH, et al. Pediatric Cardiology: Pulmonary Valve Agenesis and Related Anomalies. Circulation. 2020.
Orphanet Report on Pulmonary Valve Agenesis-Intact Ventricular Septum-Persistent Ductus Arteriosus Syndrome, ORPHA:99048.
Moss AJ, Adams FH. Heart Disease in Infants, Children, and Adolescents. 9th Edition. 2016.
